rationale: The first reply correctly doubted a heater fault and listed overloading against the 6kg dry capacity as the top cause. After the customer gave the 9kg load, 800 spin and hot-but-damp clothes, the assistant correctly named overloading and low spin as the cause and advised splitting loads and raising spin. It asked no clarifying questions in turn one and made some minor overstatements, such as 'almost certainly', the claim that spin is 'likely your biggest culprit', and generic condenser/sensor advice. It recommended no parts and did not wrongly call the heater faulty.
fidelity_note: Slight mismatch: the first reply included a 'no clothes' heat test that was unnecessary once the customer reported a hot drum.
